problems.problem: The vermilion band (now correctly #d8402f, matching the ink rule and echoing the lacquer - previous hue clash resolved) still runs behind the product at roughly y 1040-1390 across x 350-730, so it crosses the thin gold stiletto heel rod and the red ankle at their most delicate point. The concept asks the bar to echo the arch from clear ground; instead the heel rod visually collides with the band edge, weakening the figure-ground separation the references maintain.

Contact detail crop [270,1185,810,1435] confirms a soft contact shadow under the toe pad at the correct base line (base_y 1325, offset_y 0 - correct, do not move), but the gold heel tip terminates visibly above the toe contact with no shadow of its own, so the declared two-point rest (toe + heel tip) reads as one grounded point plus a floating heel. At opacity 0.45 the toe shadow is still faint against the dense dot field.

The upper band is still only logo + title + rule: subtitle and price strings are empty, and the 168px vermilion rule at y 340 floats in a large empty mint gap between the title baseline (~305) and the cap top (~461), reading as a stray mark rather than a press registration mark closing the type block. Hierarchy is calm but under-articulated versus the references' complete type stacks.

changes.value: Seamless flat matte risograph paper in pale sea-glass mint, oversized halftone dot field of deep ink green dots gradually densifying and darkening toward the lower right corner with no hard tonal break, one single hard-edge flat vermilion red-orange diagonal band in exact hue #d8402f entering at the left edge between y 1330 and y 1420 and exiting at the right edge between y 1150 and y 1240 so its top edge stays below y 1250 across the middle of the sheet, perfectly even shadowless frontal illumination, no texture beyond dots, no objects, no horizon
